summary: 音乐能力跨越文化普遍存在。文章从音乐与数学的联系转向语言和声音的研究，再通过动物比较及婴儿对音乐的反应，讨论音乐为何是人类生活的重要部分。
logic: 从数学解释转向语音证据
比较其他动物的音乐感知
以早期发展讨论音乐的作用

paragraphs.brief: 音乐普遍存在的进化难题
sentences: Music is one of the human species’ relatively few universal abilities.
音乐是人类中相对较少的普遍能力之一。
Without formal training, any individual, from Stone Age tribesman to suburban teenager, has the ability to recognise music and, in some fashion, to make it.
从石器时代的部落成员到今天住在郊区的青少年，人无需正式训练就能辨认音乐，也能以某种方式创造音乐。
Why this should be so is a mystery.
人类为何会有这种能力，仍是个谜。
After all, music isn’t necessary for getting through the day, and if it aids in reproduction, it does so only in highly indirect ways.
毕竟，日常生活并不非靠音乐不可，即使音乐有助于繁衍，这种作用也十分间接。
Language, by contrast, is also everywhere — but for reasons that are more obvious.
相比之下，语言也无处不在，但原因更为明显。
With language, you and the members of your tribe can organise a migration across Africa, build reed boats and cross the seas, and communicate at night even when you can’t see each other.
有了语言，部落成员能组织横跨非洲的迁徙、造船渡海，甚至能在看不见彼此的夜里交流。
Modern culture, in all its technological extravagance, springs directly from the human talent for manipulating symbols and syntax.
现代文化及其种种复杂技术，都直接得益于人类运用符号和句法的天赋。
Scientists have always been intrigued by the connection between music and language.
科学家总是对音乐和语言之间的联系感兴趣。
Yet over the years, words and melody have acquired a vastly different status in the lab and the seminar room.
然而，多年来，语言和音乐在实验室与学术讨论中受到的重视大不相同。

While language has long been considered essential to unlocking the mechanisms of human intelligence, music is generally treated as an evolutionary frippery — mere “auditory cheesecake”, as the Harvard cognitive scientist Steven Pinker puts it.
人们一直把语言视为揭开人类智力机制的关键，却往往把音乐当作演化的附带产物；哈佛认知科学家史蒂文·平克戏称它只是“听觉上的芝士蛋糕”。
paragraphs.gist: 几乎人人都能感知或创造音乐，然而它不像语言那样具有显而易见的生存用途，因此音乐虽普遍，却长期被视为进化的附带产物。

paragraphs.brief: 从音程比例到音乐语言联系
sentences: But thanks to a decade-long wave of neuroscience research, that tune is changing.
十年来神经科学研究不断涌现，学界的看法正随之改变。
A flurry of recent publications suggests that language and music may equally be able to tell us who we are and where we’re from — not just emotionally, but biologically.
近来一系列研究显示，音乐和语言都能帮助解释人类的本性与起源，既关乎情感，也关乎生理。
In July, the journal Nature Neuroscience devoted a special issue to the topic.
7月，《自然神经科学》杂志专门发行了一期专题专刊。

And in an article in the 6 August issue of the Journal of Neuroscience, David Schwartz, Catherine Howe and Dale Purves of Duke University argued that the sounds of music and the sounds of language are intricately connected.
杜克大学的施瓦茨、豪和珀维斯在8月6日的《神经科学杂志》撰文指出，音乐与言语的声音有着复杂而紧密的联系。
To grasp the originality of this idea, it’s necessary to realise two things about how music has traditionally been understood.
为了了解这个想法的原创性，有必要认识到音乐是如何被传统理解的两点。
First, musicologists have long emphasised that while each culture stamps a special identity onto its music, music itself has some universal qualities.
首先，音乐学家长期以来一直强调，尽管每一种文化都在其音乐上树立了特殊的身份，但音乐本身具有一些普遍的特点。
For example, in virtually all cultures, sound is divided into some or all of the 12 intervals that make up the chromatic scale — that is, the scale represented by the keys on a piano.
例如，几乎所有文化都用到半音阶十二个音程中的一部分或全部，钢琴琴键所体现的正是这个音阶。
For centuries, observers have attributed this preference for certain combinations of tones to the mathematical properties of sound itself.
几个世纪以来，观察家们将这种偏好的某些调子组合归因于声音本身的数学特性。
Some 2,500 years ago, Pythagoras was the first to note a direct relationship between the harmoniousness of a tone combination and the physical dimensions of the object that produced it.
大约2500年前，毕达哥拉斯是第一个注意到音调组合的和谐与产生它的物体的物理维度之间的直接关系的人。
For example, a plucked string will always play an octave lower than a similar string half its size, and a fifth lower than a similar string two-thirds its length.
例如，在其他条件相同的情况下，拨响一根弦，它会比长度为其一半的弦低一个八度，比长度为其三分之二的弦低五度。
This link between simple ratios and harmony has influenced music theory ever since.
简单比例和和谐之间的这种联系从那时起就影响了音乐理论。
paragraphs.gist: 新的脑科学研究把音乐与言语联系起来，这挑战了绵延两千多年的解释，即跨文化共有的悦耳音程主要来自发声体的简单数学比例。

paragraphs.brief: 语音频率与半音阶相近
sentences: This music-is-math idea is often accompanied by the notion that music, formally speaking at least, exists apart from the world in which it was created.
认为音乐本质上是数学的人也常有另一种看法，即音乐至少在形式上独立于创造它的现实世界。

Writing recently in The New York Review of Books, pianist and critic Charles Rosen discussed the long-standing notion that while painting and sculpture reproduce at least some aspects of the natural world, and writing describes thoughts and feelings we are all familiar with, music is entirely abstracted from the world in which we live.
最近，《纽约书籍评论》中，钢琴家和评论家查尔斯·罗森讨论了一个长期存在的概念，即虽然绘画和雕塑至少复制了自然世界的某些方面，写作描述了我们所有人都熟悉的想法和感觉，但音乐却完全从我们生活的世界中抽象而出。
Neither idea is right, according to David Schwartz and his colleagues.
David Schwartz和他的同事认为，这两个想法都不正确。

Human musical preferences are fundamentally shaped not by elegant algorithms or ratios but by the messy sounds of real life, and of speech in particular – which in turn is shaped by our evolutionary heritage.
他们认为，塑造音乐偏好的并非优美的算法或比例，而是生活中纷繁的声音，尤其是经过人类演化塑造的语音。
“The explanation of music, like the explanation of any product of the mind, must be rooted in biology, not in numbers per se,” says Schwartz.
“对音乐的解释，如同对任何思想产物的解释一样，必须植根于生物学，而不是数字本身。” 施瓦茨说。
Schwartz, Howe and Purves analysed a vast selection of speech sounds from a variety of languages to reveal the underlying patterns common to all utterances.
三人分析了多种语言的大量语音，寻找各种话语共有的底层模式。
In order to focus only on the raw sounds, they discarded all theories about speech and meaning, and sliced sentences into random bites.
为了专注于声音本身，他们舍去词句和意义信息，把语句随机切成短段。
Using a database of over 100,000 brief segments of speech, they noted which frequency had the greatest emphasis in each sound.
他们使用十万多段语音组成的数据库，记录每个声音中最突出的频率。
The resulting set of frequencies, they discovered, corresponded closely to the chromatic scale.
他们发现，这组频率与半音阶非常吻合。
In short, the building blocks of music are to be found in speech.
换言之，音乐的基本要素也能在日常说话声中找到。
Far from being abstract, music presents a strange analogue to the patterns created by the sounds of speech.
音乐远非抽象，而是与语言声音所创造的模式有奇怪的相似之处。
“Music, like visual arts, is rooted in our experience of the natural world,” says Schwartz.
施瓦茨(Schwartz)说，“音乐与视觉艺术一样，植根于我们对自然世界的经验。
“It emulates our sound environment in the way that visual arts emulate the visual environment.”
“视觉艺术模仿视觉环境，音乐也以类似方式模仿我们的声音环境。”
In music we hear the echo of our basic sound-making instrument — the vocal tract.
在音乐中，我们听到我们基本的声学工具——声道——的回响。
The explanation for human music is simpler still than Pythagoras’s mathematical equations: we like the sounds that are familiar to us — specifically, we like the sounds that remind us of us.
比起毕达哥拉斯的公式，还有一个更简单的解释：人喜欢熟悉的声音，尤其喜欢让人联想到人声的声音。
This brings up some chicken-or-egg evolutionary questions.
这引出了一个演化上的先后问题，类似于“先有鸡还是先有蛋”。
It may be that music imitates speech directly, the researchers say, in which case it would seem that language evolved first.
研究者说，音乐可能直接模仿了说话声；若是如此，语言似乎更早演化出来。
It’s also conceivable that music came first and language is in effect an imitation of song — that in everyday speech we hit the musical notes we especially like.
另一种可能是音乐先出现，语言实际上模仿了歌唱：人们在日常说话时会用到自己格外偏爱的那些音高。
Alternatively, it may be that music imitates the general products of the human sound-making system, which just happens to be mostly speech.
也有可能音乐模仿的是人类发声系统的各种产物，只不过其中大多是语音。
“We can’t know this,” says Schwartz.
施瓦茨说：「我们不能知道这一点。
“What we do know is that they both come from the same system, and it is this that shapes our preferences.”
“我们所知道的是，它们都来自同一个体系，正是这种体系决定了我们的偏好。”
paragraphs.gist: 研究者分析十万余段语音后发现，突出的频率与半音阶接近，提示音乐偏好可能根植于熟悉的人声，但音乐和语言谁先出现仍难判断。

paragraphs.brief: 怎样公平测试动物的音乐感
sentences: Schwartz’s study also casts light on the long-running question of whether animals understand or appreciate music.
Schwartz的研究也揭示了动物是否理解或欣赏音乐这个长期存在的问题。

Despite the apparent abundance of “music” in the natural world — birdsong, whale song, wolf howls, synchronised chimpanzee hooting — previous studies have found that many laboratory animals don’t show a great affinity for the human variety of music making.
虽然自然界里有鸟鸣、鲸歌、狼嚎和黑猩猩齐声呼叫等许多“音乐”，以往研究发现，许多实验动物对人类创作的音乐并不特别感兴趣。
Marc Hauser and Josh McDermott of Harvard argued in the July issue of Nature Neuroscience that animals don’t create or perceive music the way we do.
哈佛大学的Marc Hauser和Josh McDermott在7月的《自然神经科学》一书中说，动物不会以我们的方式创造或看待音乐。
The fact that laboratory monkeys can show recognition of human tunes is evidence, they say, of shared general features of the auditory system, not any specific chimpanzee musical ability.
他们认为，实验中的猴子能辨认人类曲调，只能说明听觉系统有某些共性，无法证明黑猩猩具备特定的音乐能力。
As for birds, those most musical beasts, they generally recognise their own tunes — a narrow repertoire — but don’t generate novel melodies like we do.
至于最富乐感的鸟类，它们一般能辨认自己那一小套曲调，却不会像人类一样创作新旋律。
There are no avian Mozarts.
也就是说，鸟类中尚未发现莫扎特。
But what’s been played to animals, Schwartz notes, is human music.
施瓦茨提醒，在这些实验中，研究者给动物播放的都是人类的音乐。
If animals evolve preferences for sound as we do — based upon the soundscape in which they live — then their “music” would be fundamentally different from ours.
如果动物和人一样，偏好自己生活的声音环境，那么它们的“音乐”从根本上就会与人类音乐不同。
In the same way our scales derive from human utterances, a cat’s idea of a good tune would derive from yowls and meows.
正如人类音阶可能源自人声，猫心目中的好曲调也可能来自各种喵叫声。
To demonstrate that animals don’t appreciate sound the way we do, we’d need evidence that they don’t respond to “music” constructed from their own sound environment.
若要证明动物不像人一样欣赏声音，还得证明它们对用自身声音环境构成的“音乐”也没有反应。
paragraphs.gist: 许多动物对人类旋律不敏感，可是检验它们有无音乐感，还须考察它们对依据自身叫声和听觉环境构成的“音乐”有何反应。

paragraphs.brief: 母婴交流连接歌唱与言语
sentences: No matter how the connection between language and music is parsed, what is apparent is that our sense of music, even our love for it, is as deeply rooted in our biology and in our brains as language is.
无论语言和音乐之间的联系如何被解读，显而易见的是，我们的音乐感，甚至我们的爱，都深深植根于我们的生物学和大脑中，和语言一样。
This is most obvious with babies, says Sandra Trehub at the University of Toronto, who also published a paper in the Nature Neuroscience special issue.
多伦多大学的Sandra Trehub也发表了一篇关于自然神经科学专题的文章。
For babies, music and speech are on a continuum.
对婴儿而言，音乐和说话的声音处于同一连续谱上。
Mothers use musical speech to “regulate infants’ emotional states”, Trehub says.
母亲用带有旋律的语调来“调节婴儿的情绪状态”。
Regardless of what language they speak, the voice all mothers use with babies is the same: “something between speech and song”.
不论她们讲什么语言，所有母亲对婴儿使用的声音是一样的：“在言语和歌曲之间”。
This kind of communication “puts the baby in a trance-like state, which may proceed to sleep or extended periods of rapture”.
这种交流会让婴儿进入一种出神般的状态，随即可能睡去，也可能长时间沉浸在愉悦中。
So if the babies of the world could understand the latest research on language and music, they probably wouldn’t be very surprised.
所以，如果世界上的婴儿能够理解最新的语言和音乐研究，他们可能不会感到很惊讶。
The upshot, says Trehub, is that music may be even more of a necessity than we realise.
Trehub说，结果显示，音乐可能比我们意识到的更有必要。
paragraphs.gist: 婴儿最能显示言语与音乐的连续性，各种语言中的母亲都会用介于说话和唱歌之间的声音安抚婴儿，调节其情绪。
